properties.name: Bolinas Lagoon – Leona Roberts body site

properties.name: Golden Gate Park police station bombing

properties.similarities: Same period as Zodiac's bomb threats; an example of Zodiac taunting police with a crime he says he didn't commit.

properties.name: 754 Stevenson Street, San Francisco – Robert Salem murder
properties.description: Robert Salem murdered April 19, 1970; 'ZODIAC' written in blood (considered copycat).

connections: Golden Gate Park police station bombing
properties.similarities: Unlike Zodiac's own killings — staged occult writing, mutilation, no vehicle, no couple — which is why investigators called it a copycat.

properties.name: Washington High School, San Francisco – Nancy Cidley body

properties.similarities: Clothing taken and dumped — the same pattern as Anstey, Roberts, and the Santa Rosa hitchhiker victims; the 'Washington' street name echoes Stine's murder street.

properties.name: Maze Road / Interstate 5 – Kathleen Johns abduction

properties.similarities: Weekend, night, full moon, near water, Navy-style dress and crew cut — all match the Zodiac M.O.; the only survivor to escape him with her child.
properties.geographic: Stanislaus County, near Patterson; two-lane Maze Road off I-5.

properties.name: Pine Hill, Tamalpais Valley – Isobel Watson attack

properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: White Chevy, Friday night, black-rimmed glasses, short-bladed knife — the Ferrin/Johns vehicle and eyewear pattern recurring.
properties.geographic: Marin County, Tamalpais Valley; residential hillside.

properties.name: Lake Merced, San Francisco – Linda Dudley body

properties.similarities: Body near water — the recurring Zodiac geography (Lake Herman, Blue Rock, Berryessa, Bolinas, Tahoe).

properties.similarities: Body in water, autumn equinox timing — one of the many linked female homicides CI&I compiled.

properties.name: Vallejo Police Department

properties.financial_legal: Housed the Ferrin case files; later the site of the department shake-up after Mayor Douglas's 1970 press conference.
properties.similarities: Same pairing as Napa PD — a police HQ close to the phone booth the killer used.

properties.geographic: Vallejo, in front of the Solano County Sheriff's Office, within sight of the Ferrin home.

properties.name: Napa Police Department

properties.similarities: Same police-near-phone-booth pairing as Vallejo PD and Joe's Union Station.

properties.summary: Pay phone at 1231 Main St used by Zodiac after the Berryessa stabbings; a palm print was lifted.

properties.similarities: Phone booth near a police station; ~27 mi from the attack site.
properties.geographic: Napa, four and a half blocks from Napa PD.

properties.name: Solano County Sheriff's Office
properties.description: Near Darlene Ferrin's Virginia Street home; visible from Joe's Union Station booth.
properties.summary: Solano County SO headquarters, directly across from the Joe's Union Station phone booth and next to the Ferrin house — the agency that took over from Benicia PD on the Jensen-Faraday and Ferrin cases.
properties.financial_legal: Zodiac's 12:40 a.m. call was placed in front of this building; the caller may have watched the building while he spoke.
properties.similarities: Like Napa SO, it became a rival investigative shop with its own theory of the case.
properties.geographic: Vallejo, near Virginia Street and Tuolumne.

properties.name: Benicia Police Department
properties.description: First responders to Lake Herman Road murders.
properties.summary: Benicia PD whose patrol car was flagged down by Stella Borges at 11:19 p.m. Dec 20, 1968; Capt. Daniel Pitta and Officer William T. Warner reached gate #10 three minutes later and found Faraday dying and Jensen dead.
properties.financial_legal: Crime occurred in unincorporated Solano County, outside Benicia jurisdiction; evidence was handed to the Solano County Sheriff's Office.
properties.similarities: Small first-responder agency like Napa PD — the kind of department Zodiac's jurisdictional hopping was designed to fragment.

properties.name: San Francisco Hall of Justice
properties.description: SFPD headquarters and homicide detail; Toschi & Armstrong's office.
properties.summary: Bryant Street Hall of Justice, fourth-floor homicide detail, where Toschi and Armstrong kept the Zodiac cabinet and where the Stine case and Zodiac squad were run.
properties.financial_legal: Site of the 1978 Toschi forgery inquiry and his transfer to Pawn Shop Detail; later the point from which files were shipped to Sacramento DOJ in 1981.
connections: San Bruno Postal Service Crime Lab
properties.similarities: Command post like Napa SO and Vallejo PD, but the only one that became the center of the political controversy.

properties.name: Napa County Sheriff's Office
properties.description: Investigated Lake Berryessa attack (Det. Sgt. Ken Narlow).
properties.summary: Napa County SO where Det. Sgt. Ken Narlow ran the Berryessa investigation, took casts of Zodiac's size 10½ Wing Walker boot prints, and kept his own 'best bet' suspect (Don Andrews) file locked in a desk.
properties.financial_legal: Napa had three homicides in ten days in 1969 and requested a DOJ investigator; Narlow's suspect files were kept separately from SFPD's.
properties.similarities: Sister command post to Vallejo PD and SF Hall of Justice, but one that stayed closer to its own suspect theory (Andrews) than Toschi's (Starr).

properties.name: San Bruno Postal Service Crime Lab
properties.description: John Shimoda authenticated Zodiac letters here.
properties.summary: Postal Service crime lab in San Bruno where John Shimoda first authenticated the April 1978 'I am back with you' letter, saying 'That's your man. He's back.'
properties.financial_legal: Shimoda later reversed his authentication under pressure (working 'only from photocopies') and ended his five-year relationship with SFPD in July 1979.
properties.similarities: Parallel to Sacramento CI&I — a handwriting/forensic stop on every genuine Zodiac letter.
properties.geographic: San Bruno, San Mateo County, near SFO.

properties.name: Pleasanton, CA – LA Times letter postmark
properties.description: Zodiac's March 13, 1971 letter to the Los Angeles Times was mailed from Pleasanton.
properties.summary: Pleasanton postmark on Zodiac's 16th letter — the first non-San Francisco postmark on a Zodiac letter — mailed with double postage and inverted Roosevelt stamps to the LA Times.
properties.financial_legal: Why Pleasanton? It suggested Zodiac traveled or lived outside the city; the letter itself was the one that said 'I am crack proof' and claimed the Riverside activity.
properties.similarities: Same odd-postage, inverted-stamps signature as the other letters — a postmark clue rather than a murder site.

properties.name: San Rafael, CA – 'Red Phantom' letter postmark
properties.description: Zodiac's July 8, 1974 letter to the Chronicle was postmarked San Rafael.
properties.summary: San Rafael postmark on the July 8, 1974 'Red Phantom' letter — the odd protest against anti-feminist columnist Count Marco, written in unusually neat handprinting with long swooping tails.
properties.financial_legal: Count Marco quit the Chronicle after fifteen years because of the threat, moved to Hawaii, and later returned.
properties.similarities: Like the Pleasanton postmark, evidence that Zodiac mailed letters from outside SF; San Rafael is near Starr's brother's home.
properties.geographic: Marin County, north of the Golden Gate.

properties.name: Alameda County – Badlands letter postmark
properties.description: Zodiac's May 8, 1974 Badlands letter was postmarked in Alameda County.
properties.summary: Alameda County postmark on the May 8, 1974 letter protesting the Chronicle's ad for the film Badlands — 'In 1959 most people were killing time. Kit & Holly were killing people.'
properties.financial_legal: Notably, the spelling and punctuation were correct and no new victims were claimed — a change from earlier letters.
connections: Pleasanton, CA – LA Times letter postmark
properties.similarities: Same non-SF postmark pattern as Pleasanton and San Rafael.

properties.name: San Francisco – most Zodiac letters
properties.description: Most Zodiac letters bore San Francisco postmarks.
properties.summary: San Francisco as the default mailing city for the bulk of the Zodiac correspondence — addressed 'Please Rush to Editor' to the Chronicle, with double postage and inverted Roosevelt stamps.
properties.financial_legal: Most letters mailed from SF; a few from Pleasanton, San Rafael, and Alameda County — suggesting travel or a second residence.
properties.similarities: The SF default is the exact inverse of the murder pattern: attacks in Vallejo/Napa/SF, letters almost always from SF.

properties.name: Sacramento – CI&I Questioned Documents
properties.description: Sherwood Morrill's office; authenticated Zodiac letters.
properties.summary: Sherwood Morrill's office, where every Zodiac letter was authenticated and where the Riverside and Starr samples were compared.

connections: San Bruno Postal Service Crime Lab
properties.similarities: The evidentiary backstop for every other location — the place the letters were tied to the crimes.

properties.geographic: Santa Rosa; trailer court, off wheels.

properties.financial_legal: Forrest Pines condominium development under construction; Lass worked at the Sahara Hotel in Stateline.
properties.similarities: Near water and isolated — same victim geography as Lake Berryessa and Bolinas Lagoon.

properties.name: Presidio, San Francisco
properties.description: Zodiac fled into the Presidio after killing Paul Stine.
properties.summary: Army base one and a half blocks north of Cherry and Washington; Zodiac fled into it after shooting Stine and vanished.
properties.financial_legal: Federal military reservation, open around the clock with almost no security in 1969.
properties.similarities: Adjacent to the Stine scene as Lake Herman Road is to the pumping station — a dark boundary the killer could cross on foot.
properties.geographic: San Francisco; Sixth Army headquarters; dense undergrowth.

properties.name: Julius Kahn Playground, San Francisco
properties.description: Zodiac crossed this playground after the Stine murder.
properties.summary: Playground the stocky man crossed after the Stine shooting, crouching against the stone wall before working south to his car.
properties.financial_legal: City park.
properties.similarities: Same pattern as the Presidio — a public green space used as cover immediately after an attack.
properties.geographic: San Francisco, Presidio Heights edge of the Presidio.

properties.name: Golden Gate Bridge
properties.description: Zodiac could have fled north into Marin via the bridge.

properties.name: Mare Island Naval Shipyard, Vallejo
properties.description: Naval base; ciphers sent to Naval Intelligence here.

properties.name: Golden Gate Theatre, San Francisco
properties.description: Where the 1971 Zodiac film played; movie contest box.
properties.summary: Golden Gate Theatre on Market, where a low-budget Zodiac film ran for one week and a contest box was set up in the lobby with a man crouched inside to read entries — and where the Roper Agency's suspect reportedly attended three times.
properties.financial_legal: Producer Tom Hansen pledged $100,000 to the Roper Agency for capture; the contest invited 25-word 'I Believe The Zodiac Killed Because…' entries.
properties.similarities: Like the silent-film interest in Andrews and Bernell, the theater as a site where Zodiac's obsession with movies could surface.
properties.geographic: San Francisco, Market Street near Civic Center.

properties.name: St. Francis Hotel, San Francisco
properties.description: Paul Stine picked up Zodiac near here on Oct 11, 1969.
properties.summary: Union Square hotel where Zodiac stood watching the cab ranks before hailing Paul Stine's taxi.
properties.financial_legal: Hotel; taxi zone in front.
properties.similarities: Staging area before an attack, as Terry's parking lot was before the Ferrin chase.
properties.geographic: San Francisco, Union Square at Powell and Post.

properties.name: Geary Theatre, San Francisco
properties.description: Theater district where Zodiac hailed Stine's cab.
properties.summary: Geary Theatre, where the audience of Hair poured out at 9:30 p.m. Oct 11, 1969, while Zodiac watched the cab ranks from the doorway of Harold's Books next door.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: A crowded public entertainment block — the urban equivalent of a lovers' lane as ambush ground.
properties.geographic: San Francisco, Geary Street theater district.

properties.name: Curran Theatre, San Francisco
properties.description: Next door to Geary; 1978 Mikado production.
properties.summary: Curran Theatre at 445 Geary Street — next door to the Geary — where the 1978 Mikado played only a few feet from where Zodiac hailed Stine's cab; Toschi flagged the ad for surveillance of the mail.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: Zodiac's lyrics came from The Mikado, and the Lamplighters were rehearsing it thirteen blocks from the Stine murder a week before — the theater is the coincidence.
properties.note: Base file places Curran essentially on top of Geary; keep but do not plot both as separate points without visual jitter.

properties.name: Harold's Books and Magazines, San Francisco
properties.description: Zodiac stood under the awning here watching cabs.
properties.summary: Harold's Books and Magazines, whose red-striped awning Zodiac stood under while watching the Luxor, DeSoto, Veteran's, City, and Yellow cabs converge on the theaters the night of Oct 11, 1969.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: The bookshop awning is Zodiac's urban version of the Lake Herman Road tree cover — cover while he watched.

properties.name: KGO-TV / Channel 7 studio, San Francisco
properties.description: Jim Dunbar's talk show; 'Sam' calls to Melvin Belli, Oct 22, 1969.
properties.summary: Channel 7 studio where Jim Dunbar hosted the two-hour call-in with Melvin Belli on Oct 22, 1969 — 35 calls from 'Sam', 12 heard on air, the longest nine minutes.
properties.financial_legal: None; the voice was later identified as a Napa State Hospital patient.
connections: St. Vincent de Paul Thrift Shop, Daly City
properties.similarities: Like the Belli letter and the Examiner's surrender plea, part of Zodiac's long conversation with the media.
properties.geographic: San Francisco, Nob Hill/Union Square area.

properties.name: St. Vincent de Paul Thrift Shop, 6726 Mission St, Daly City
properties.description: Belli waited here for Zodiac on Oct 22, 1969; Zodiac stood him up.
properties.summary: Daly City thrift shop where Melvin Belli waited 45 minutes on Oct 22, 1969 for the caller 'Sam' — who named this spot at 10:30 a.m. and then never appeared.
properties.financial_legal: The 'least secret secret meeting in history' — Belli was followed by police, who were followed by TV crews.
properties.similarities: Like the Fairmont rooftop suggestion, a location named by a caller that produced no killer; 'Sam' was later traced to Napa State Hospital.

properties.name: Moskowite Corners General Store (Lake Berryessa)
properties.description: Stocky man asked directions away from the lake on the day of the Berryessa attack.
properties.summary: Store across from Pearce's Chevron where a nervous stocky man frantically asked the quickest way out of the lake area on the day of the Berryessa stabbings.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: Post-attack exit point, as Joe's Union Station was for Blue Rock Springs.

properties.name: Rancho Monticello Resort, Lake Berryessa
properties.description: Rangers launched rescue boats from here after the stabbings.
properties.summary: Resort where a Chinese fisherman reported the stabbings and from which Rangers Land and White launched by boat.
properties.financial_legal: Concession resort at the lake.
properties.similarities: Rescue staging point, like the Benicia patrol cars converging on Lake Herman Road.

properties.name: Lake Berryessa Park Headquarters
properties.description: Two miles south of the attack site.

properties.name: Benicia Water Pumping Station
properties.description: Gate #10 where Faraday and Jensen were parked.

properties.name: Lake Herman Road
properties.description: Isolated road between Vallejo and Benicia; first Zodiac murder site.

properties.name: Lake Berryessa
properties.description: Napa County lake; Shepard-Hartnell attack.

properties.name: Clear Lake
properties.description: Near Lake Berryessa; mentioned in the 340-symbol cipher solution.

properties.name: Russian River
properties.description: Teresa Matthews' body found near here, Feb 24, 1979.

properties.name: Lake Merced, San Francisco
properties.description: Near where Linda Dudley's body was found.

properties.name: San Francisco
properties.description: Primary Zodiac letter destination and Stine murder site.

properties.name: Vallejo
properties.description: First three Zodiac attacks; Darlene Ferrin's home.
properties.summary: City of the first three attacks and both Ferrin-Mageau and Jensen-Faraday murders, plus the Ferrin home and the Joe's Union Station phone booth; the geographic center of the case's first phase.
properties.financial_legal: Ferrin house cost $9,500; the department's handling of the Ferrin case was publicly criticized by Mayor Douglas in 1970.
properties.similarities: Like Santa Rosa later, a mid-sized city that supplied both victims and a suspect's basement.
properties.geographic: Solano County, north shore of San Pablo Bay.

properties.name: Napa
properties.description: Napa PD received Zodiac call; school-bus threat area.

properties.name: Benicia
properties.description: Near Lake Herman Road crime scene.

properties.name: Santa Rosa
properties.description: Cluster of possible Zodiac-linked murders; Starr's later home.
properties.summary: Sonoma County city where the linked female homicides and hitchhiker murders clustered in the 1970s, where Starr's mother bought a house in 1975, and where he returned after his 1977 release.
properties.context_label: Narrative hub city / suspect later home
properties.financial_legal: Starr's family bought the Santa Rosa house in 1975; his 1971 trailer search produced no admissible evidence and his 1975 child-molestation conviction sent him to Atascadero until 1977.
properties.similarities: The 1970s clusters here mirror Vallejo's 1968-69 pattern — young women, remote roads, water, weekend nights, clothing kept.

properties.name: Sacramento
properties.description: CI&I / Morrill's handwriting lab; Carol Hilburn murder.

properties.name: San Jose
properties.description: Snoozy & Furlong murders, Aug 3, 1969.
properties.summary: Site of the Aug 3, 1969 Snoozy–Furlong knife murders, later linked by autopsy to the 1971 Bilek killing; ruled out as Zodiac's work because he always claimed credit.

properties.name: Oakland
properties.description: Oakland PD received 2 a.m. 'Zodiac' call, Oct 22, 1969.
properties.summary: Oakland PD took the 2:00 a.m. Oct 22, 1969 call from a man claiming to be Zodiac and demanding F. Lee Bailey or Melvin Belli on Channel 7.

properties.name: Berkeley
properties.description: DeLouise's psychic impression of Zodiac's residence.
properties.summary: Where psychic Joseph DeLouise placed Zodiac's residence — 'I don't see him from Vallejo … I do get strong impressions he is living in Berkeley.'

properties.name: Riverside
properties.description: Cheri Jo Bates murder; 'Riverside Connection'.
properties.summary: Southern California city of the Cheri Jo Bates murder, the RCC library desk-top poem, and the three 'Bates had to die' letters — the 'Riverside Connection' that Morrill eventually authenticated as Zodiac printing.
properties.context_label: Narrative hub city / possible early murder
properties.financial_legal: A suspect was held and released on bail; the local man was never charged with the Bates murder; Morrill ruled him out as Zodiac by handwriting in November 1970.
properties.similarities: Knife murder of a young student, with a letter campaign to the press — the closest structural parallel to the Bay Area Zodiac attacks.

properties.name: Los Angeles
properties.description: LA Times received Zodiac letter, March 1971.
properties.summary: The LA Times received Zodiac's sixteenth letter, postmarked Pleasanton, on March 13, 1971 — the first to a paper outside San Francisco.

properties.name: Santa Cruz
properties.description: Trailside Killer attacks; possible Zodiac link investigated.
properties.summary: Site of the 1981 Trailside Killer attacks; KTVU suggested a Zodiac link, but David Carpenter was later cleared by handwriting, fingerprints, and jail records.

properties.name: Saratoga
properties.description: Villa Montalvo; Kathy Bilek murder.
properties.summary: Town adjacent to Villa Montalvo, where Kathy Bilek was killed Easter 1971; Karl Werner pleaded guilty but was ruled out as Zodiac.

properties.name: Palo Alto
properties.description: Palo Alto Times received 'Zodiac' call, Oct 1969.
properties.summary: The Palo Alto Times received a call from a man claiming to be Zodiac — 'I had to leave San Francisco because I'm too hot there' — taken seriously enough to arm-guard 25 school buses.

properties.name: San Rafael
properties.description: Starr's brother lived here; 'Red Phantom' postmark.
properties.summary: Marin County city named by Toschi as relevant to a suspect; also the postmark on the July 8, 1974 'Red Phantom' letter.

properties.name: Tamalpais Valley
properties.description: Isobel Watson attack, April 7, 1972.
properties.summary: Marin community where Isobel Watson was stabbed April 7, 1972 by a man in a white Chevy who offered her a ride.

properties.name: Vacaville
properties.description: California Medical Facility; schoolteacher's threatening letters.
properties.summary: Solano County town where a young schoolteacher received four anonymous breathing calls and two handprinted letters ('I watch you a lot and call you a lot…'), while a dark-green four-door Ford sat afternoons behind her apartment complex.
properties.financial_legal: CI&I called the handprinting 'very, very contrived,' an attempt to imitate an eighth- or ninth-grader.
properties.similarities: Anonymous handprinted threats and stalking phone calls — the same media-taunting pattern as the Zodiac letters, but at a private victim.

properties.name: Dixon
properties.description: Schoolteacher fled here; letters followed.
properties.summary: Town near Sacramento where the Vacaville schoolteacher fled to her boyfriend on Silveyville Road; a letter followed her there and another followed her to her parents' house in El Sobrante.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: Letters that pursue a victim from place to place — the opposite of Zodiac's public letters to editors.
properties.geographic: Solano County, near I-80 northeast of Vacaville.

properties.name: Cordelia
properties.description: Schoolteacher worked here; 'Phantom of Cordelia'.
properties.summary: Solano County town where the Vacaville schoolteacher taught seventh and eighth grade and where, years later, women reported a white Chevy tailgating them on moonlit nights — the local name for that driver was 'the Phantom of Cordelia.'
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: White Chevy stalking women — the exact Ferrin-Johns-Watson pattern recurring years later.
properties.geographic: Solano County, near I-80 between Vallejo and Fairfield.

properties.name: St. Helena
properties.description: Near Lake Berryessa; suspect search.
properties.summary: Napa Valley town where a search warrant was issued and a man's house searched in connection with the Berryessa case — 'a number of unidentified articles were removed for inspection,' nothing came of it.
properties.financial_legal: Search warrant issued; articles removed; no charges.
properties.similarities: A suspect cleared by search — same shape as the June 4, 1971 Starr trailer search.

properties.name: Angwin
properties.description: Pacific Union College; Shepard & Hartnell.
properties.summary: Napa County hill town and home of Pacific Union College, where Cecelia Shepard and Bryan Hartnell were students and where the 1969 foot searches for Lynda Kanes began.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: A student town near water — same pairing as Hogan High and the Jensen home, or RCC and the Bates murder.
properties.geographic: Napa County, Howell Mountain above the valley.
properties.note: Base file places Angwin and Pacific Union College at the same coordinates; they are effectively the same site.

properties.name: Rutherford
properties.description: Bryan and Cecelia drove through here.
properties.summary: Napa Valley town Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shepard drove through on their way to Lake Berryessa.

properties.name: Bodega Bay
properties.description: Starr skin-dived here; lived nearby in 1969.
properties.summary: Sonoma coast town where Bob Starr skin-dived and where he claimed to have been with three or four friends on July 4, 1969 — an alibi Sergeant Lynch said he checked and accepted.
properties.financial_legal: None; the alibi is what kept Starr off Lynch's list in 1969.
properties.similarities: Water-adjacent like every Zodiac site, but as an alibi rather than a crime scene.
properties.geographic: Sonoma County coast, north of San Francisco.

properties.name: Lakeport
properties.description: Darlene's sister Pam followed here in later years.
properties.summary: Lake County town on Clear Lake where Darlene Ferrin's sister Pam was followed years after the murder; the same man, she said, delivered the familiar line: 'This is the Zodiac speaking.'
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: The Ferrin family crank calls continuing decades later — the same pattern as the 1:00 a.m. breathing calls of July 4, 1969.

properties.name: Livermore
properties.description: Fechtel & Shane bodies dumped off highway.
properties.summary: Where Cathy Fechtel and Michael Shane were killed and dumped off a highway, nineteen days before the 1973 Winter Solstice.

properties.name: Hayward
properties.description: Possible Zodiac victim site.
properties.summary: Listed by Graysmith among the possible Zodiac victim sites in the linked-homicide appendix.

properties.name: Monterey
properties.description: Possible Zodiac victim site.
properties.summary: Listed in the appendix as a possible Zodiac victim site.

properties.name: Marysville
properties.description: Brenda Merchant murder site.
properties.summary: Where Brenda Merchant was stabbed Feb 1, 1974, listed among the linked female homicides.

properties.name: San Mateo
properties.description: Bomb threat caller claimed Zodiac, 1978.
properties.summary: Its police operator took the May 5, 1978 call claiming a Zodiac bomb in the Transamerica Building.

properties.name: Modesto
properties.description: Kathleen Johns first noticed she was being followed here.
properties.summary: Central Valley city where Kathleen Johns first noticed a junky car on her tail as she drove toward Highway 132; the Modesto Bee was also the only paper to report her car being torched.
properties.financial_legal: The Bee's small report is how Zodiac could have known the car burned — relevant if his later claim to have done it was borrowed rather than earned.
properties.similarities: Like Pleasanton or San Rafael, a place with meaning only because of a coincidence of timing and press coverage.

properties.name: Patterson
properties.description: Near Maze Road / I-5 abduction site.
properties.summary: West Stanislaus town next to the Maze Road/I-5 shoulder where Kathleen Johns's wheel came off and her abductor picked her and her baby up.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: Highway abduction — same pattern as the Santa Rosa hitchhiker cases and the Watson attack.

properties.name: Fresno
properties.description: Kathleen Johns drove through.
properties.summary: Waypoint on Kathleen Johns's night drive up Highway 99 with her baby.

properties.name: Merced
properties.description: Kathleen Johns drove through.
properties.summary: Waypoint on Kathleen Johns's night drive up Highway 99.

properties.name: Bakersfield
properties.description: Kathleen Johns drove through.
properties.summary: Waypoint on Kathleen Johns's night drive before she turned onto Highway 132.

properties.name: San Diego
properties.description: Andrews claimed he had been here.
properties.summary: Southern city where Don Andrews claimed to have stayed — the only place in Southern California he acknowledged, while denying ever having been in Riverside.
properties.financial_legal: None; his denial about Riverside is what makes the San Diego admission interesting.
connections: Don Andrews' engine shop, San Francisco
properties.similarities: Like Starr's Bodega Bay claim, a suspect's self-reported whereabouts used to place or clear him.
properties.geographic: San Diego County, far Southern California.

properties.name: Deer Lodge, Montana
properties.description: Prison Zodiac claimed to have escaped from (Berryessa costume story).
properties.summary: Montana prison Zodiac claimed to have escaped from at the Berryessa stabbing — 'I'm an escaped convict from Deer Lodge, Montana. I've killed a prison guard there. I have a stolen car and nothing to lose. I'm flat broke.'
properties.financial_legal: The claim was false — Hartnell later recalled the hooded man had a stolen car story but no prison escape was traced to him.
properties.similarities: A lie told to establish a reason not to be argued with — same conversational tactic as the kidnapper's lie to Kathleen Johns.

properties.name: Ogden, Utah
properties.description: Distribution point for 103,700 pairs of Wing Walker boots.
properties.summary: Distribution point for 103,700 pairs of Wing Walker boots shipped to Air Force and Navy installations on the West Coast.

properties.name: Merrill, Wisconsin
properties.description: Weinbrenner Shoe Co. – makers of the Wing Walker boot uppers.
properties.summary: Weinbrenner Shoe Company, maker of the Wing Walker boot uppers found in the Berryessa footprint casts.

properties.name: Avon, Massachusetts
properties.description: Maker of the Wing Walker soles (circle printing).
properties.summary: Maker of the Wing Walker soles, whose small circular printing appeared between heel and sole in the Berryessa casts.

properties.name: Syracuse, New York
properties.description: Syracuse Research Institute – psycholinguistic report on Zodiac.
properties.summary: Syracuse Research Institute, author of the secret psycholinguistic report profiling Zodiac from nineteen of his letters.

properties.name: Kent State, Ohio
properties.description: American Cryptogram Association convention where Graysmith's cipher solution was validated.
properties.summary: American Cryptogram Association convention where Graysmith's solution to the 340-symbol cipher was validated in 1979.

properties.name: Chicago, Illinois
properties.description: Psychic Joseph DeLouise's base.
properties.summary: Base of psychic Joseph DeLouise, whose visions of Zodiac brought him to the Bay Area at his own expense in January 1970.

properties.name: Washington, D.C.
properties.description: CIA and NSA – asked to crack Zodiac ciphers.
properties.summary: CIA and NSA, both asked to break the Zodiac ciphers; NSA reportedly confirmed a message was present but could not read it.

properties.name: Lubbock County, Texas
properties.description: Region where the phrase 'fiddle and fart around' is common (Zodiac phrasing clue).
properties.summary: Region where the antiquated phrase 'fiddle and fart around' is common — a phrasing clue that led investigators to suspect Zodiac was older than assumed.

properties.name: Troutdale, Oregon
properties.description: Bryan Hartnell's parents' home; he drove from here to help Cecelia pack.
properties.summary: Oregon town where Bryan Hartnell had been visiting his parents; he drove back to Angwin specifically to help Cecelia Shepard pack for her transfer to UC Riverside.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: The road trip that made the Berryessa picnic happen at all — the randomness that Narlow stressed in ruling out prior surveillance.
properties.geographic: Multnomah County, Oregon, east of Portland.

properties.name: Loma Linda, California
properties.description: Cecelia Shepard's parents' home.

properties.name: Point Pleasant, West Virginia
properties.description: Silver Bridge collapse – DeLouise's 1967 prediction.
properties.summary: Silver Bridge collapse of Dec 15, 1967, one of DeLouise's claimed predictions.

properties.name: Chappaquiddick, Massachusetts
properties.description: Ted Kennedy car accident – DeLouise's 1969 prediction.
properties.summary: Ted Kennedy's 1969 car accident, the prediction that made DeLouise's national reputation.

properties.name: Indianapolis, Indiana
properties.description: Air crash at 3:31 – DeLouise's 1969 prediction.
properties.summary: Air crash at 3:31, another of DeLouise's claimed predictions.

properties.name: Loma Linda
properties.description: Cecelia Shepard's parents' home.
properties.summary: Southern California town where Cecelia Shepard spent the summer with her parents before returning to PUC; her mother and father were at her bedside when she died Sept 29, 1969.
properties.financial_legal: None.
properties.similarities: The Shepard family's Adventist community in Loma Linda mirrors the PUC community in Angwin.

properties.name: Refugio Beach / Gaviota – Domingos-Edwards murder site
properties.description: Isolated beach off southbound US-101, 3 mi south of Gaviota Tunnel, near Refugio Creek mouth; crude shack where the bodies were stacked and set alight. Murdered June 4, 1963.
properties.summary: Site of the June 4, 1963 double homicide of Lompoc High seniors Robert Domingos and Linda Edwards — Graysmith's candidate for Zodiac's first killing.
properties.financial_legal: No robbery motive; .22 Winchester Super-X brass and four boxes of ammo (lot TL21) left behind; ammunition traced to Vandenberg AFB exchange.
connections: Silver Spray Apartments, Ocean Beach, San Diego – Swindle murder site
properties.similarities: Precut clothesline; one victim ordered to bind the other at gunpoint; victim couple at water's edge — pattern repeated at Lake Berryessa six years later.
properties.geographic: Santa Barbara County coast; 20 mi west of Santa Barbara.

properties.name: Silver Spray Apartments, Ocean Beach, San Diego – Swindle murder site
properties.description: Ocean-front patio with low retaining wall; sniper's nest ~50 ft away behind a concrete projection. Murdered Feb 5, 1964.
properties.summary: Sniper murder of Navy Radioman Johnny Ray Swindle and his bride Joyce — the second Southern California 'sweetheart slayer' killing.
properties.financial_legal: Wallet and watch taken — possibly to simulate robbery; seven shell casings recovered; Remington-Peters hollow-point .22 LR.
properties.similarities: Couple ambushed from concealment at water's edge; point-blank coup de grâce to each victim — same double pattern as Gaviota.

properties.name: Doctor's Hospital, San Diego
properties.description: Hospital where Johnny Ray Swindle died at approximately 11:00 P.M. Feb 5, 1964.
properties.summary: Where the surviving Swindle victim was taken after the Ocean Beach shooting; he died about three hours after arrival.
connections: Silver Spray Apartments, Ocean Beach, San Diego – Swindle murder site
properties.similarities: Like Queen of the Valley (Berryessa) and SF General — hospitals Zodiac victims were taken to.

properties.name: Terracina Drive (between 3680 and 3692), Riverside – Bates body site
properties.description: Unlit gravel driveway between two vacant frame houses where Cheri Jo Bates was found face down at 6:28 A.M. Oct 31, 1966.
properties.summary: The precise spot where Cheri Jo Bates's body was discovered — 75 yards from her disabled VW, near the RCC library.
properties.financial_legal: Purse with 56 cents left beneath the body; paint-spattered Timex watch found 10 ft away; typewriter identified as Royal portable, Elite type.
connections: Riverside City College – Cheri Jo Bates murder site
Pigeon Pass, Riverside – Nov 22, 1966 UCR coed attack
properties.similarities: Knife killing of a lone female; body left between two empty houses, as Gaviota's body pair was left in a shack.
properties.geographic: Riverside; off Terracina just east of the RCC library annex.

properties.name: Pigeon Pass, Riverside – Nov 22, 1966 UCR coed attack
properties.description: Dark uphill road above Riverside where a 19-year-old UCR coed was choked and told 'Shall I kill you now?' Nov 22, 1966 — three weeks after Bates's murder.
properties.summary: A near-fatal attack with the same Good Samaritan ruse as Bates's; the same man had given her a ride near the UCR library, then picked her up again.
connections: Riverside City College – Cheri Jo Bates murder site
properties.similarities: Good Samaritan ruse; assailant described as '35, 5'9", chunky, protruding stomach.'

properties.name: Highgrove, Riverside
properties.description: Neighborhood where the Nov 22, 1966 UCR coed staggered after fleeing her attacker.
properties.summary: Where the choking survivor reached safety; her purse and books were taken.
connections: Pigeon Pass, Riverside – Nov 22, 1966 UCR coed attack
properties.similarities: Like Lake Berryessa victim Hartnell crawling toward Knoxville Road.

properties.name: Lompoc, California – Domingos-Edwards home town
properties.description: Lompoc High School seniors Robert Domingos and Linda Edwards lived here; both graduated (posthumously honored) in 1963.
properties.summary: The pair left Lompoc for what was meant as a senior Ditch Day at Santa Barbara Beach; instead they drove to the Gaviota turnout.
properties.financial_legal: Robert had a job lined up at Richfield Oil; couple planned a November wedding.
connections: Refugio Beach / Gaviota – Domingos-Edwards murder site
properties.similarities: School-age student couple, as at Lake Herman Road and Lake Berryessa.
properties.geographic: Santa Barbara County; ~1 hr NW of Santa Barbara.

properties.name: Vandenberg Air Force Base
properties.description: SAC base near Lompoc; investigators traced the four boxes of TL21 .22 LR ammunition from the Gaviota shack to its base exchange.
properties.summary: Probable purchase point for the ammunition left at the Domingos/Edwards murder — the earliest military-linked forensic thread in the extended case.
properties.financial_legal: No price sticker on any of the four boxes; SAC base exchange distinguished from the Santa Barbara sporting-goods store by sticker practice.
connections: Refugio Beach / Gaviota – Domingos-Edwards murder site
properties.similarities: Military-exchange sourcing echoes the Wing Walker shoes bought at bases in 1969.

properties.name: March Air Force Base, Riverside
properties.description: SAC base just outside Riverside; the Wing Walker-type Leavenworth-prison shoe was available at its base exchange and matched the footprint near Cheri Jo Bates's body.
properties.summary: Riverside military connection for the size-8-to-10 shoe print found at the Bates scene.
connections: Riverside City College – Cheri Jo Bates murder site
properties.similarities: Military-issue footwear appearing at two separate Zodiac-linked scenes (Riverside 1966, Lake Berryessa 1969).

properties.name: Cal Poly San Luis Obispo – Allen attended
properties.description: State college where Arthur Leigh Allen enrolled Sept 18, 1954, again 1959, and graduated with a B.E. Dec 15, 1961; All-American diver and Central California trampoline and spearfishing champ.
properties.summary: Allen's principal college. He met Phil Tucker and others here who later supplied details about his weapons and fantasies.
properties.financial_legal: Attended on the G.I. Bill Jan–Mar 1961.
connections: Cal Poly Pomona – Cheney, Panzarella, Ron Allen attended
properties.similarities: Like Kaczynski, a withdrawn technical student with an aptitude for codes and weapons.

properties.name: Cal Poly Pomona – Cheney, Panzarella, Ron Allen attended
properties.description: Southern California campus where Donald Cheney, Sandy Panzarella, and Ron Allen shared a house in 1962; Leigh Allen visited here June 1963, days before the Gaviota murders.
properties.summary: The college house where Allen showed a machete, slammed it into the counter, and tried to scare the roommates — just before Robert Domingos and Linda Edwards were killed.
properties.financial_legal: Shared rented four-bedroom house with two other students.
connections: Refugio Beach / Gaviota – Domingos-Edwards murder site
properties.similarities: Just a few hours' drive from Gaviota; timing places Allen in the region for the first extended crime.

properties.name: Hemet Mental Hospital (Hemet, CA)
properties.description: State mental hospital ~20 miles from Riverside where Allen worked briefly in 1960 before becoming a psychiatric teacher at Atascadero.
properties.summary: One of Allen's short-lived institutional jobs and the closest he came professionally to a psychiatric career — and to the Riverside crime scene.
connections: Riverside City College – Cheri Jo Bates murder site
properties.similarities: Institutional psychiatric employment — the kind of low-visibility post that would have enabled movement between jurisdictions.

properties.name: Pomona – Donald Cheney home
properties.description: Home of Donald Lee Cheney and family, where Cheney recognized the Zodiac composite in a Pomona newspaper in 1970 and finally went to Pomona PD in 1971.
properties.summary: The place where Cheney's memory of Allen's New Year's Day 1969 'Zodiac' conversation was triggered by a newspaper sketch and later by the LA Times letter.
properties.financial_legal: Cheney was working at Fluor engineering in Pomona when he first saw the Zodiac sketch; later took a job at a La Verne paper mill.
connections: Cal Poly Pomona – Cheney, Panzarella, Ron Allen attended
properties.similarities: Like the Ron/Karen Allen tip in 1971 — a civilian-initiated lead rather than a police discovery.

properties.name: Science Dynamics, Torrance
properties.description: Computer bookkeeping business owned by Sandy Panzarella where Cheney worked and where Manhattan Beach PD detectives Amos and Langstaff first took the Zodiac tip on July 15, 1971.
properties.summary: The business address where the most productive lead in the entire case (Cheney/Panzarella naming Allen) was first reported to police.
properties.financial_legal: Panzarella sold Science Dynamics and used the proceeds to acquire the RKO-Radio Pictures film library.
properties.similarities: A business address as tip origin — reminiscent of the blue-collar job leads the VPD later followed.

properties.name: Xenia, Ohio – Joe Allen Johnson arrest
properties.description: Ohio city where the FBI arrested Joe Allen Johnson in early Nov 1970 on the Radetich warrant; SFPD dropped the Radetich charge for lack of evidence Jan 9, 1971.
properties.summary: The out-of-state end point of the initial Radetich investigation — a false lead that cost the SFPD nearly six months.
properties.financial_legal: Charged with interstate flight, armed robbery, burglary; Radetich murder charge dropped for lack of corroboration.
connections: 600 block Waller Street, San Francisco – Radetich murder scene
properties.similarities: Like the 'Sandy' suspect in the Gaviota murders — a false suspect who consumed investigative resources.

properties.name: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.description: Chestnut stucco two-story house on the east side of Fresno Street; Allen occupied the basement for decades, then lived alone there after his mother's death in 1989.
properties.summary: Specific address of the 'Bob Starr' residence in the existing set. Allen's basement was searched under warrant Feb 14, 1991 — pipe bombs, formulas, a Zodiac Sea Wolf watch, and a forged DOJ clearance letter recovered.
properties.financial_legal: Held as mother's house; Allen could have used the upper floors but stayed in the basement. 1991 search warrant sealed, then unsealed in part; address never published before 1991.
connections: 216 Aragon Street, Vallejo – Ron and Karen Allen home
553 Wallace Street, Vallejo – Robbie Lee Moncure apartment
properties.similarities: Basement — Zodiac's 'death machine stored in my basement' phrase. Pipe bombs found Feb 1991.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; east side of Fresno Street near Illinois Street.

properties.name: 216 Aragon Street, Vallejo – Ron and Karen Allen home
properties.description: Off Columbus Parkway; the home of Allen's brother and sister-in-law, who in 1971 called Toschi and Armstrong directly, dissatisfied with the VPD investigation.
properties.summary: Where the key 1971 corroborating family interviews took place; also on the route the Blue Rock Springs killer could have used to escape back into Vallejo.
properties.financial_legal: Karen told police Allen hated his mother despite her financial support; Bernice bought him cars and boats.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
Blue Rock Springs Golf Course parking lot (Ferrin-Mageau attack)
properties.similarities: Just off the escape route from Blue Rock Springs; distance to the crime scene is less than a mile.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; cul-de-sac off Columbus Parkway, near Blue Rock Springs.

properties.name: 45 Fresno Street, Vallejo – William White home
properties.description: Home of William Langdon White, Allen's neighbor seven doors down; White saw Allen return home on the day of the Berryessa stabbings — Allen's alibi witness.
properties.summary: Allen told Toschi he had spoken to White after returning home Sept 27, 1969, but 'neglected to tell' Sergeant Lynch. White died Nov 4, 1969, seventeen days after Lynch's interview.
properties.financial_legal: White was a longtime business representative for Butchers' Union Local 532 — a man likely to notice a bloody knife.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: A key witness dying soon after giving information recurs throughout the case.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; Fresno Street, seven houses from Allen.

properties.name: 553 Wallace Street, Vallejo – Robbie Lee Moncure apartment
properties.description: Apartment house across from the Ferrin apartment at 560 Wallace; home of Robbie Lee Moncure, Darlene's friend who owned the white '68 Mercury Cougar that a Terry's waitress saw following her.
properties.summary: The building where Darlene's friend 'Lee' — a slim 25-year-old, not Allen — lived and may have observed the older stocky man staking out Darlene.
properties.financial_legal: Moncure worked at Kresge's and Mare Island Naval Station; traded a 1960 Impala for the Cougar April 1969.
properties.similarities: The white Cougar is the wrong vehicle for the Berryessa tire tracks (57" wheelbase width); likely a separate 'Lee' from the Zodiac suspect.

properties.name: 1545 Broadway, Vallejo – Allen's boat storage
properties.description: Lot where Allen kept a 22-foot sailboat on a trailer (CA license NE3725) and a 10-foot open sailboat (CF 9127 FD); searched under warrant Feb 13, 1991.
properties.summary: Secondary cache point outside the Fresno Street home; Bawart thought Zodiac's souvenirs might be hidden underwater or in one of the trailers.
properties.financial_legal: One boat described as 'adapted … runs on unknown fuel' — mother had bought both.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
Sunset Trailer Park, 2963 Santa Rosa Avenue – Allen trailer
properties.similarities: Like the Bodega Bay trailer, an unsearched alternate cache — the same gap that doomed the 1972 Santa Rosa warrant.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; 1545 Broadway, near the Napa River straits.

properties.name: The Plunge, 801 Nebraska Street, Vallejo
properties.description: Vallejo community swimming center shared by high school and junior college students; Allen was a popular lifeguard and platform diver here 1950–51 and after.
properties.summary: Where Allen first became known as a champion diver and where he met Bobbie, the diver he later described to Cheney as the one woman he had ever cared about.
properties.financial_legal: Allen's mother considered his weight gain a personal failing after his diving career ended.
connections: Vallejo Junior College / Vallejo Senior High School
32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Like Kemper and Gacy, a locally known athlete whose later obesity disguised him.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; 801 Nebraska Street, opposite Vallejo High.

properties.name: Vallejo Junior College / Vallejo Senior High School
properties.description: Amador Street campus; Allen attended both and was a member of the wrestling team, graduating 1951; earned an AA from Vallejo JC in 1957.
properties.summary: Allen's earliest school, and the site of the swimming team where Robert Emmett Rodifer was manager — the 'Robert Emmett the Hippie' of the 408 cipher's trailing characters.
connections: Cal Poly San Luis Obispo – Allen attended
properties.similarities: Robert Emmett Rodifer's presence here may explain the 'Robert Emmett the Hippie' reading of the 408's null tail.

properties.name: Elmer Cave Elementary School, 770 Tregaskis, Vallejo
properties.description: Where Sergeant John Lynch interviewed Allen at 4:05 P.M. Oct 6, 1969 — eight days after the Berryessa stabbings; Allen was working as a part-time custodian.
properties.summary: Site of the earliest documented police interview with Allen as a Zodiac suspect. Lynch's report runs to about 110 words; he never recorded who had named Allen.
properties.financial_legal: Part-time janitor; also a janitor at Benjamin Franklin Jr. High around this time.
connections: Benjamin Franklin Jr. High School, 501 Starr Avenue, Vallejo
properties.similarities: A school workplace fits the same profile Zodiac exploited in his 'school bus' threats; custodial roles gave him access to children.

properties.name: Benjamin Franklin Jr. High School, 501 Starr Avenue, Vallejo
properties.description: Allen worked as a janitor here in 1969; the school sits near a Zodiac victim's home.
properties.summary: One of Allen's two 1969 custodial posts, and the second address tying him to school access during the year of the Northern California murders.
connections: Elmer Cave Elementary School, 770 Tregaskis, Vallejo
864 Beechwood Avenue, Vallejo – Mike Mageau home
properties.similarities: School access to children.
properties.geographic: Vallejo; Starr Avenue, north of Hogan High.

properties.name: Harry Wogan's Service Station, Vallejo
properties.description: Allen's employer as a mechanic in the late 1960s; Wogan's three small children drew Allen's unwanted attention and Wogan let him go.
properties.summary: One of several service stations where Allen worked — a job that gave him access to customer cars overnight, as Phil Tucker's Corvair was left at the Richfield station.
properties.financial_legal: Allen left or was let go around 1970; later told Bawart he had left to attend Sonoma State.
properties.similarities: Access to many cars overnight — possibly supporting the 'many vehicles' signature of the case.

properties.name: Arco station, 640 Broadway, Vallejo
properties.description: Where Allen worked about six months until April 1969 (fired, drunk); Phil Tucker's brown 1965 Corvair was left on the lot in summer 1969 to be sold.
properties.summary: Key location for the Ferrin murder vehicle theory: Tucker's brown Corvair was at this station mid-summer 1969, when the killer drove an 'older brown car similar to a Corvair.'
properties.financial_legal: Allen fired April 1969; invoice for Tucker's Corvair repair could not be located.
connections: Sonoma Auto Parts Store, 248 West Napa Street, Sonoma
Blue Rock Springs Golf Course parking lot (Ferrin-Mageau attack)
properties.similarities: Brown car similar to Ferrin's bronze Corvair — the exact description Mageau gave.

properties.name: Ace Hardware, 1131 Tennessee Street, Vallejo
properties.description: Allen's later retail job (Jan–Nov 1980); Graysmith watched him here in 1980; the sign on the wall used a felt-tip print closely resembling the Zodiac letters.
properties.summary: Where Graysmith obtained fresh handprinting samples (via a clipboard photograph) and where he exchanged eye contact with Allen on Tennessee Street.
properties.financial_legal: Paid $5.35/hr; Allen complained he 'hated working for a living.'
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: The felt-tip sign at the store matched Zodiac's lettering closely enough for Morrill to say 'the closest Zodiac lettering I've seen.'

properties.name: Spectro Chrome Graphics, Benicia
properties.description: Allen's job as warehouse supervisor Nov 1980 – May 1981; fired after he destroyed a roll-down door with a forklift.
properties.summary: One of the last jobs before Allen went on disability; the firing is one of the six grievances Bawart counted as motive against 'authority.'
properties.financial_legal: About $5/hr; destruction estimated at $2,300.
properties.similarities: Firing-as-motive — same pattern as the Pinole refinery dismissal.

properties.name: Sonoma Auto Parts Store, 248 West Napa Street, Sonoma
properties.description: Where Allen worked 1974–1980; in 1974 Jim Silver brought Bryan Hartnell here to hear Allen's voice, and Hartnell said it matched the hooded attacker.
properties.summary: Critical identification point — the Lake Berryessa survivor's in-person voice identification of Allen.
properties.financial_legal: Allen was rejected for lack of advancement; complained he only got one day off.
properties.similarities: The voice of the attacker — described by Hartnell as 'some type of drawl' — was matched to Allen here.

properties.name: Union Oil refinery, Pinole
properties.description: Where Allen worked as a junior chemist (Sept 8, 1970 – May 5, 1972); Toschi, Armstrong, and Mulanax interviewed him here Aug 4, 1971.
properties.summary: Site of the single most productive police interview in the case — Toschi and Armstrong first saw the Zodiac wristwatch here and heard Allen volunteer the bloody-knife and Riverside facts.
properties.financial_legal: Fired May 5, 1972 — Allen believed the SFPD interview had caused the termination.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Workplace interview — same tactic used later at Ace Hardware and (via Bawart) at the Vallejo home.
properties.geographic: Pinole; Contra Costa County, on San Pablo Bay.

properties.name: Union 76 garage, Rodeo
properties.description: Where Allen applied for a garage job April 20, 1970, while still working at the Pinole refinery — a clue to his restlessness before the Button Letter.
properties.summary: Small additional workplace lead; not developed by police.
properties.similarities: Like the Wogan's, Arco, and Ace Hardware jobs — Allen's pattern of short-lived employment.

properties.name: Valley Springs Elementary School
properties.description: Calaveras County school where Allen taught 4th grade and PE in 1967–68; fired in spring 1968 after a parent complained about his handling of her daughter.
properties.summary: The teaching post where he muttered 'Titwillow' and made inappropriate advances to 11- and 12-year-old girls — behavior that fed his later threats about school buses.
properties.financial_legal: Terminated for 'improper conduct' and 'exaggeration of teaching credentials'; Allen filed a resignation and moved on.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Teaching jobs — like the elementary-school connection in his school-bus threats.

properties.name: Mountain Town School (Sierras)
properties.description: Foothill school where Allen also briefly taught in the 1960s, according to his own job applications.
properties.summary: Another Calaveras-area post; like Valley Springs, an elementary school in a rural, lightly supervised area.
properties.financial_legal: Listed on his 1966 Calaveras Unified application.
connections: Salt Point Ranch / Fort Ross (Sonoma Coast)
properties.similarities: Wilderness school setting echoes the lovers'-lane geography of the crimes.
properties.geographic: Sierra foothills; Calaveras / San Andreas area.

properties.name: Santa Rosa School, Atascadero
properties.description: Elementary school near the state hospital where Allen taught fourth grade and PE from 1959 to 1963 — including the year of the Gaviota murders. Not to be confused with Santa Rosa city.
properties.summary: One of the earliest posts; about 2 hours from Gaviota and 20 minutes from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo.
properties.financial_legal: Listed on applications from 1966 onward as 'four years' teaching experience.'
connections: Cal Poly San Luis Obispo – Allen attended
properties.similarities: Teaching career places Allen in Southern California during the earliest attributed murders.

properties.name: Camp La Honda YMCA, La Honda Gulch
properties.description: YMCA camp where Allen worked from Sept 4, 1967 until June 7, 1968 — including three unexplained absences Feb 5–7, 1968.
properties.summary: Camp counselor post in the Santa Cruz Mountains; the three-day absence doesn't match any known Zodiac murder but shows his pattern of unaccounted-for travel.
properties.financial_legal: Absence slip said 'personal business,' altered to 'school business.'
connections: Vallejo Junior College / Vallejo Senior High School
Salt Point Ranch / Fort Ross (Sonoma Coast)
properties.similarities: Camp / counselor role — the same kind of access to children as the teaching and custodial jobs.
properties.geographic: San Mateo County; Santa Cruz Mountains.

properties.name: Travis Air Force Base
properties.description: Military base near Fairfield where Allen taught 7th and 8th grade in 1963–64 and where Wing Walker boots were sold at the base exchange; also the source of one of the early 'school bus threat' responses in the Bay Area.
properties.summary: Post-military employment for Allen (through his father's dependent privileges) and a source of the footwear later found at Lake Berryessa.
properties.financial_legal: Base-exchange purchases restricted to active-duty and dependents, each with photo and thumbprint I.D.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Air Force connection — some 103,700 pairs of Wing Walkers shipped to Ogden, Utah for distribution to West Coast installations.

properties.name: Rohnert Park – Sonoma State University
properties.description: Where Allen studied biology and chemistry 1970–1982 (BA awarded June 2, 1982).
properties.summary: Allen's later college; his biology thesis (chipmunks) explains the animal parts in his freezer and the dissection permits.
properties.financial_legal: On the G.I. Bill; later on state disability.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Biology study — like Kemper's zoology interests and the animal-torture profile.

properties.name: Atascadero State Hospital for the Criminally Insane
properties.description: Where Allen was committed 1975–77 (and where he had briefly taught in 1961); a 1975 polygraph administered here was later disputed as inconclusive because of Thorazine and Valium in Allen's system.
properties.summary: The state hospital where Allen reportedly passed a polygraph and later forged a 'cleared' letter in the print shop; also the source of the 1971 claim that he 'hoped Zodiac would write a letter' to prove his innocence.
properties.financial_legal: Bawart later argued Allen drugged himself for the polygraph.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: The institution as both a place to learn techniques and a place to forge evidence.

properties.name: Sunset Trailer Park, 2963 Santa Rosa Avenue – Allen trailer
properties.description: Specific address of the off-wheels Universal trailer (Slot A-7) searched by Toschi and Armstrong Sept 14, 1972; trailer repaneled shortly before the search.
properties.summary: Location where the 1972 search warrant was served. Vaseline, dildos, sadomasochistic pornography, animal parts in the freezer, and a Lake Berryessa map were found — but no direct evidence.
properties.financial_legal: Warrant signed by Judge James E. Jones Jr.; Allen returned 45 minutes after police arrived; the trailer was one of several he kept.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Search of a secondary residence while the primary was left alone — the jurisdictional gap Graysmith called the case's central error.

properties.name: Burson, California – Allen's 1967 P.O. box address
properties.description: Calaveras County town to which Allen's 1967 driver's license address is listed (a P.O. box in Burson).
properties.summary: One of several addresses used by Allen in the mid-1960s; sits between Valley Springs (school) and the Salt Point alibi location.
connections: Salt Point Ranch / Fort Ross (Sonoma Coast)
properties.similarities: Like the Bodega Bay trailer and the (rumored) hidden fourth trailer — a location never fully searched.

properties.name: Salt Point Ranch / Fort Ross (Sonoma Coast)
properties.description: Where Allen claimed he had gone scuba diving on Sept 26–27, 1969 instead of Lake Berryessa — his alibi location for the Berryessa stabbings.
properties.summary: Repeated alibi site: Allen told Sergeant Lynch he had gone to Salt Point rather than the lake, and later told Toschi and Mulanax the same.
properties.financial_legal: No record of the serviceman-and-wife Allen said he met at the coast.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Water-based alibi; same pattern of 'I was diving' for Lake Herman Road (Big Sur) and Blue Rock Springs (Bodega Bay).
properties.geographic: Sonoma County coast; near Fort Ross.

properties.name: Paso Robles
properties.description: Where Allen stayed with friends after his Aug 31, 1977 release from Atascadero.
properties.summary: Intermediate residence between Atascadero release and his return to Vallejo in Jan 1978; where he wrote Toschi: 'If I can ever be of any help …'.
properties.financial_legal: Living with friends; shortly after applied to Benicia Import Auto Service as a mechanic.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Another short-lived residence outside the Bay Area that was never searched.

properties.name: Grass Valley, California
properties.description: Where Allen and Cheney fly-fished; also the area of the 1971 killings Cheney cited as re-igniting his suspicions about Allen.
properties.summary: Fishing area and a temporal clue: Cheney says 'the 1971 killings in the Grass Valley area had also brought my suspicions to a focus.'
connections: Sonoma Auto Parts Store, 248 West Napa Street, Sonoma
properties.similarities: Like Clear Lake and Lake Berryessa — fishing areas overlapping the regions where Zodiac victims were found.

properties.name: 600 block Waller Street, San Francisco – Radetich murder scene
properties.description: Where Officer Richard Radetich was shot three times through the driver's-side window of his patrol car at 5:25 A.M. Friday, June 19, 1970.
properties.summary: One .38 slug recovered; the case was later tied to Zodiac through his April 20, 1970 letter hint that he shot 'a man sitting in a parked car with a .38.'
properties.financial_legal: Radetich lay in state at City Hall; over 1,000 paid respects; Johnson charged then cleared Jan 9, 1971.
connections: Scott and Haight Streets, San Francisco – Radetich prior citation
Xenia, Ohio – Joe Allen Johnson arrest
properties.similarities: Water-named street (Waller) — same Lake/Springs/River naming pattern as the earlier scenes.

properties.name: Scott and Haight Streets, San Francisco – Radetich prior citation
properties.description: Where Radetich had stopped to write a citation a few minutes before his murder.
properties.summary: The immediate pre-murder location; the shooting happened a block away at Waller.
connections: 600 block Waller Street, San Francisco – Radetich murder scene
properties.similarities: Short interval between citation and ambush — same 'blitz' pattern as Lake Herman Road.

properties.name: Northpoint Theater, San Francisco
properties.description: Where The Exorcist opened Dec 26, 1973 and drew 60,000 admissions before New Year; the crowd noise and fainting were themes Zodiac picked up in his Jan 29, 1974 letter.
properties.summary: The commercial success of The Exorcist gave Zodiac a reason to break his three-year silence; the SFPD briefly circulated surveillance photos of the crowd.
properties.financial_legal: Avery's 'Weird Goings-On at the Movies' ran on the front page Jan 11, 1974.
properties.similarities: The Exorcist served as the trigger the same way the 1932 film The Most Dangerous Game had inspired the original M.O.
properties.geographic: San Francisco; Northpoint and Powell, Fisherman's Wharf.

properties.name: Washington and Locust Streets, San Francisco – Paul Hom robbery
properties.description: Where Yellow Cab driver Paul Hom picked up a passenger at 11:00 P.M. Sept 30, 1969, was forced into the Presidio, and robbed of $35 without being killed.
properties.summary: Twelve days before the Stine killing — a probable rehearsal for the Oct 11 murder. Captain Marty Lee called it 'amazing similarity of M.O.'
properties.financial_legal: Robber took $35; released Hom unharmed. Described as 24, 135 lb — likely a different man.
connections: Maple Street, San Francisco – Fouke sighting
Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
properties.similarities: Same taxi-victim template as the Stine murder; timing suggests either rehearsal or the actual killing was copied from this robbery.

properties.name: Maple Street, San Francisco – Fouke sighting
properties.description: Where Officer Donald Fouke saw the stocky man turn north off Jackson Street and walk into the Presidio shortly after the Stine murder.
properties.summary: The exact turn point where the most detailed surviving description of Zodiac was observed — 35–45 years old, 5'10", 180–200 lb, dark blue windbreaker, pleated brown pants, crew cut, glasses.
properties.financial_legal: Fouke wrote his memo Nov 12, 1969; it was never added to the amended circular.
connections: Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
properties.similarities: The route into the Presidio that Zodiac claimed in his Nov 9, 1969 letter.

properties.name: 500 9th Avenue (Allen Arms apartments), San Francisco
properties.description: Stine's unfinished fare destination — an apartment complex whose name contains 'Allen.'
properties.summary: Tom Voigt's observation: the address on Stine's dispatch was 500 9th Avenue, Apt. #1 — the Allen Arms. If Zodiac chose the specific fare, this was a route into his surname.
properties.financial_legal: Stine never arrived; the fare was reassigned at 9:58 P.M.; the meter reading allowed Toschi to backtrack to Geary & Mason.
connections: Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
properties.similarities: The name-game pattern that also shows up in victim names (David Arthur Faraday; Arthur Dean Ferrin; Lori Lee Kursa; Maureen Lee Sterling; Kim Wendy Allen).

properties.name: 320 2nd Avenue, San Francisco – 'Arthur Allen, student' apartment
properties.description: Unfurnished apartment rented by an 'Arthur Allen, student,' four and a half blocks from the Stine murder site.
properties.summary: Graysmith's specific clue tying an 'Arthur Allen' to the Stine neighborhood; not proved to be Leigh Allen, but consistent with the name-game pattern.
properties.financial_legal: Rental ad appeared in 1969.
connections: Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
properties.similarities: Four and a half blocks from the murder — same proximity pattern as Allen to Blue Rock Springs.

properties.name: Letterman General Hospital, Presidio
properties.description: Army hospital inside the Presidio where Donna Lass worked as a staff nurse from February to June 1970 — months after Zodiac fled into the Presidio after the Stine murder.
properties.summary: Convergence point: Zodiac's escape route ran through the Presidio, and one of his possible later victims worked inside it.
properties.context_label: Possible victim workplace / escape route terminus
properties.financial_legal: Lass left for Lake Tahoe in June 1970 to work at the Sahara Hotel and Casino; disappeared Sept 6, 1970.
connections: 225 Mallorca Way, San Francisco – Donna Lass residence
properties.similarities: The Presidio as both escape route and victim workplace — same site-specific coincidence as the Ferrin home's proximity to the phone booth.

properties.name: San Francisco General Hospital
properties.description: Where Radetich died (8:02 P.M. June 19, 1970) and where Charles Jarman died two days after his Jan 25, 1970 shooting.
properties.summary: Hospital for two extended-case victims.
connections: 600 block Waller Street, San Francisco – Radetich murder scene
1752 Fell Street, San Francisco – Jarman murder site
properties.similarities: Hospital-site death of a Zodiac victim; parallel to Queen of the Valley (Berryessa) and Doctor's Hospital (San Diego).

properties.name: Queen of the Valley Hospital, Napa
properties.description: Where Hartnell and Shepard were taken after the Lake Berryessa stabbings; Shepard died here Sept 29, 1969.
properties.summary: The receiving hospital for the Berryessa victims — about 45 minutes from the lake.
properties.similarities: Same-day receiving hospital — pattern used to determine whether the killer intended the victims to die.

properties.name: South Lake Tahoe Police Department
properties.description: Took the initial missing-person report on Donna Lass; searched her apartment (found 'exceptionally clean'), found her Camaro parked nearby.
properties.summary: The originating agency for the Lass disappearance — the case that would later connect to Zodiac's 'peek through the pines' card.
properties.financial_legal: Family hired a private investigator; about $5,000 in expenses.
connections: 225 Mallorca Way, San Francisco – Donna Lass residence
properties.similarities: A local department outside the Zodiac case's normal jurisdiction, which slowed the tie-in to the Bay Area investigation.
properties.geographic: South Lake Tahoe; El Dorado County.

properties.name: San Joaquin County Sheriff's Office
properties.description: Where Kathleen Johns was taken the day after her March 22, 1970 abduction; she identified the Zodiac wanted poster on their wall.
properties.summary: The secondary agency for the Johns case (Patterson PD was primary). Johns spent much of the next day here.
connections: Maze Road / Interstate 5 – Kathleen Johns abduction
properties.similarities: Cross-jurisdiction investigation — same friction as the Bay Area agencies.

properties.name: Patterson Police Department
properties.description: Where Kathleen Johns reported the abduction at about 2:30 A.M. March 23, 1970, and where she saw the Zodiac composite.
properties.summary: The originating police agency for the Johns case; the officer's handling of her report became a source of controversy.
connections: Maze Road / Interstate 5 – Kathleen Johns abduction
properties.similarities: Like the VPD — a small agency whose handling of a Zodiac-related case was later questioned.

properties.name: Napa State Hospital
properties.description: Where 'Sam' (the caller to the Dunbar/Belli show Oct 22, 1969) was later identified as a patient.
properties.summary: The institution that closed the 'Sam' hoax — after two hours of live calls to KGO-TV.
connections: St. Vincent de Paul Thrift Shop, 6726 Mission St, Daly City
properties.similarities: 'NSH' initials were also floated as a possible solution to the trailing EBEORIETEMETHHPITI anagram.

properties.name: Langley Porter Neuropsychiatric Institute, UCSF
properties.description: Where Allen was reportedly evaluated along with UC Berkeley psychiatrists May 1973 – Sept 1974, and where his 'potentially violent, dangerous, capable of killing' finding was recorded.
properties.summary: One of the institutions consulted by Dr. Thomas Rykoff and the parole office after the first mental-health evaluation of Allen.
properties.financial_legal: Reports contributed to the 1991 search-warrant application.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Same cluster of institutions used for Bundy, Kemper, Bianchi evaluations.

properties.name: 1752 Fell Street, San Francisco – Jarman murder site
properties.description: Presidio Heights address where Yellow Cab driver Charles Jarman was shot Jan 25, 1970 — one of several Yellow Cab killings that police initially considered Zodiac-related.
properties.summary: The Jarman murder was eventually solved (Robert Bromell confessed) and was NOT Zodiac — the closest the case came to a wrongful attribution.
properties.financial_legal: Yellow Cab offered a $1,000 reward; Bromell's fingerprints matched; he confessed and led police to the discarded wallet.
connections: Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
properties.similarities: Same victim type (Yellow Cab, Presidio Heights, single shot to the head) but no shirt swatch, no call, no letter — the signature absence that cleared Zodiac.

properties.name: U-Save Market, Santa Rosa – Lori Lee Kursa
properties.description: Santa Rosa market where 13-year-old Lori Lee Kursa was last seen Nov 21, 1972; her body was found Dec 12 in a ravine 55 ft off Calistoga Road, neck broken, nude, frozen.
properties.summary: First of the Santa Rosa victims in Graysmith's linked series; killed elsewhere, dumped at Calistoga Road — 100 yards from where Jeannette Kamahele's body was later found.
properties.financial_legal: Clothes missing; no sexual assault evident; body frozen in a ravine.
connections: Calistoga Road – Santa Rosa shallow grave
Franz Valley Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
properties.similarities: Clothes kept, near water, dumped in a ravine, killed elsewhere — the linked-murder pattern.

properties.name: Redwood Ice Skating Rink, Steele Lane, Santa Rosa
properties.description: Where 12-year-olds Maureen Sterling and Yvonne Weber were last seen Friday, Feb 4, 1972; their skeletons were found Dec 28, 1972 off Franz Valley Road.
properties.summary: First two Santa Rosa JC-area girls in the linked series; both hitchhikers.
properties.financial_legal: Clothing kept; one gold earring taken from each.
connections: Franz Valley Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
properties.similarities: Both 12-year-olds; hitchhiking; bodies in a ravine 66 ft below the road; same dump site as Carolyn Davis.

properties.name: Bell Avenue Freeway entrance, Santa Rosa – Kim Wendy Allen
properties.description: Where 19-year-old Kim Wendy Allen was last seen hitchhiking north on 101 at 5:20 P.M. March 4, 1972.
properties.summary: Santa Rosa JC student whose body was found the next day in a creek bed 20 ft from Enterprise Road — strangled with white clothesline, wrists and ankles bound.
properties.financial_legal: Possibly raped; inconsistent with the known Zodiac M.O. Clothing and one gold earring kept.
connections: Bennett Valley Road / Enterprise Road, Santa Rosa – Kim Wendy Allen body
Franz Valley Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
properties.similarities: Bondage pattern (spread-eagled) and clothes kept — the closest structural match to Lake Berryessa's binding.
properties.geographic: Santa Rosa; Bell Avenue freeway entrance.

properties.name: Bennett Valley Road / Enterprise Road, Santa Rosa – Kim Wendy Allen body
properties.description: Creek bed 20 ft from Enterprise Road where Kim Wendy Allen's body was found March 5, 1972.
properties.summary: The single most linked Santa Rosa body site — 'ENTERPRISE' appeared at the bottom of the Bates confession letter (as the Riverside paper name) and here at the body dump.
properties.financial_legal: White clothesline used to strangle; rope sent to FBI, no trace evidence.
connections: Bell Avenue Freeway entrance, Santa Rosa – Kim Wendy Allen
properties.similarities: Water's edge. 'Enterprise' recurs as a Zodiac choice of word (Confession letter, Riverside Press-Enterprise).

properties.name: Cotati on-ramp, Highway 101 – Jeannette Kamahele
properties.description: Where 20-year-old Jeannette Kamahele was last seen hitchhiking north on 101 near the Cotati on-ramp April 25, 1972; body found July 6, 1979, hands and ankles bound to her neck with white clothesline.
properties.summary: Last of the linked Santa Rosa victims in time (body discovered 1979) but disappeared in 1972; her body was 100 yards from Kursa's.
properties.financial_legal: White clothesline wrapped four times around her neck — same material as the Shepard/Hartnell ligatures.
connections: Calistoga Road – Santa Rosa shallow grave
Franz Valley Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
properties.similarities: Clothesline binding directly parallels Berryessa; body in a shallow grave near a ravine.

properties.name: Los Guilucos School for Girls – Zodiac sighting Nov 16, 1970
properties.description: About 8 miles from Santa Rosa; a female employee stopping at Pythian Way and Sonoma Highway saw a stocky man step from the brush and grab her door handle.
properties.summary: Witness sighting that produced one of the most Zodiac-consistent late descriptions: 35, light receding hair, dark-rimmed glasses, navy-blue jacket.
connections: Redwood Ice Skating Rink, Steele Lane, Santa Rosa
properties.similarities: Same grab-the-door-handle approach the killer used on Kathleen Johns.

properties.name: Pythian Way and Sonoma Highway
properties.description: Intersection where the Los Guilucos employee was grabbed; she accelerated away.
properties.summary: The exact intersection of the near-attack; same day as the Nov 16, 1970 Riverside/Bates conference.
connections: Los Guilucos School for Girls – Zodiac sighting Nov 16, 1970
properties.similarities: Roadside ambush; like the Johns abduction and the Blue Rock Springs attack, the killer approached the driver's side.

properties.name: Mark West Springs Road
properties.description: Rural road that forks into Franz Valley Road and Porter Creek Road — the two Santa Rosa body-dump sites.
properties.summary: Graysmith's 'fork in the road' parallel to Lake Herman Road and Blue Rock Springs; the killer chose left or right on different occasions.
connections: Franz Valley Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
Porter Creek Road – Santa Rosa body dump site
Calistoga Road – Santa Rosa shallow grave
properties.similarities: A right-or-left fork choice — Graysmith's same fork motif at Lake Herman Road and Blue Rock Springs.
properties.geographic: Sonoma County; northwest of Santa Rosa.

properties.name: Melvin Belli residence (Telegraph Hill penthouse)
properties.description: Belli's San Francisco penthouse, at 1228 Montgomery Street on Telegraph Hill; Zodiac called here on Dec 18, 1969, reaching the housekeeper.
properties.summary: The residence where Zodiac tried to reach Belli and got the housekeeper instead: 'I can't wait. Today's my birthday. I've got to kill!' — Dec 18 was Leigh Allen's birthday.
