properties.financial_legal: Zodiac gave his real birthday in the call — the single most important clue in the Belli relationship.
properties.similarities: Same Belli-as-confidant dynamic as the A.M. San Francisco call-in show four months earlier.

properties.name: Melvin Belli office (Montgomery Street)
properties.description: Belli's law office where his secretary opened the Dec 20, 1969 letter with the swatch of Stine's shirt after it was forwarded from his house.
properties.summary: Where the Belli Christmas letter was finally opened and forwarded to Toschi and Armstrong.
properties.financial_legal: Letter arrived at Belli's home Dec 23 while he was in Munich; forwarded here.
properties.similarities: Like the Chronicle newsroom, a mail-routing node where Zodiac's letters surfaced after delay.
properties.geographic: San Francisco; Montgomery Street financial district.

properties.name: Manhattan Beach Police Department
properties.description: Where detectives Richard Amos and Art Langstaff first took the Cheney/Panzarella tip on July 15, 1971 and where Armstrong followed up July 26.
properties.summary: The originating agency for the most productive single tip in the case; a Los Angeles-area department with no prior Zodiac involvement.
properties.context_label: Originating agency for the key tip
properties.financial_legal: Amos and Langstaff requested Starr's 'yellow sheet' from Sacramento CI&I; Armstrong traveled down to verify the story.
properties.similarities: Out-of-area tip — parallel to Mulanax receiving the note from the Concerned Citizen two years earlier.
properties.geographic: Manhattan Beach; LA County South Bay.

properties.name: San Francisco State University – 1993 Zodiac conference
properties.description: Where Judge George T. Choppelas convened an April 26, 1993 panel on Zodiac with Conway, Bawart, Rita Williams, and Robert Graysmith.
properties.summary: The first time Vallejo and the SFPD publicly named Arthur Leigh Allen as the prime suspect — three years after his death.
properties.financial_legal: None — the D.A. would not file against a dead man.
properties.similarities: The first quasi-official posthumous naming; documented in KTVU coverage that night.

properties.name: Vallejo Police Department headquarters (1991 re-opening)
properties.description: VPD headquarters where Conway and Bawart prepared the February 1991 search warrant and the July 1991 arrest scenario for Allen.
properties.summary: Operations hub for the last major Zodiac investigation — the one that produced the pipe bombs, the Sea Wolf watch, and the Bawart thirty-point report.
properties.financial_legal: Prepared case for Sonoma County D.A. Mike Nail; Nail declined to file against a dead man; case left open.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: The department's final push — but twenty years after the fact, with most physical evidence destroyed.

properties.name: Santa Clara County Jail (Ralph Spinelli)
properties.description: Where Ralph Spinelli was held Dec 14, 1990 on robbery charges when he named Allen as Zodiac in exchange for a deal.
properties.summary: A second independent tipster naming Allen — Spinelli claimed Allen told him he would shoot a San Francisco cabdriver just before the Stine murder.
properties.financial_legal: Spinelli sought to have all charges dropped; Conway and Bawart refused; eventually named Allen through his public defender.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: Like Cheney's tip, a civilian-initiated naming of Allen; possibly the second time Allen had been named to police by someone he had threatened.

properties.name: Sonoma County Jail (Allen)
properties.description: Where Allen was held in 1975 and 1977 on child-molestation charges; the 1975 booking photo showed him wearing a Zodiac watch.
properties.summary: Site of the March 3, 1975 booking that put Allen on Sergeant John Burke's radar — the moment a Zodiac watch was formally noted in a police file.
properties.financial_legal: Held on PC 288 charges; served 150 days at Sonoma County Jail between Atascadero commitments.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: The watch entered the police record only through an unrelated booking — the same accidental discovery pattern as the Vallejo 1991 search.

properties.name: Central Park, New York – Zodiac II shooting
properties.description: Where Larry Parham, 30, was shot in the chest while sleeping on a bench behind the Central Park band shell on the evening of June 21, 1990.
properties.summary: The fourth Zodiac II victim and the one that brought the NYPD to 49 detectives; a note covered by a rock cited astrological symbols.
properties.financial_legal: A thumbprint was lifted from the note; it eventually linked to Heriberto 'Eddie' Seda.
properties.similarities: Lovers' lane replaced by a park bench; the astrological-signs pattern is unique to Zodiac II.

properties.name: Woodhaven / 87th Road, Queens – Zodiac II first shooting
properties.description: Queens block where Joseph Proce, 78, was shot May 31, 1990 — the first Zodiac II victim; the shooting site straddled the Brooklyn-Queens border.
properties.summary: The first Zodiac II shooting; the 'wrong borough' fact let the NYPD develop the theory that Zodiac II was imitating the original Zodiac's cross-jurisdiction tactics.
properties.financial_legal: Proce died of infection after the shooting; a bullet from the scene was linked later by ballistics.
connections: Central Park, New York – Zodiac II shooting
East New York / Pitkin Avenue, Brooklyn – Zodiac II residence
properties.similarities: Cross-jurisdiction confusion (Brooklyn vs. Queens) — parallel to the multiple-county structure of the original Zodiac case.

properties.name: East New York / Pitkin Avenue, Brooklyn – Zodiac II residence
properties.description: Apartment building where Heriberto 'Eddie' Seda lived with his mother and sister; site of the June 18, 1996 shootout that finally identified Zodiac II.
properties.summary: Residence of the man who killed three and wounded others in 1990 while calling himself Zodiac — arrested after shooting his own half-sister.
properties.financial_legal: Thirteen homemade guns, pipe bombs, and multiple knives seized; three simultaneous bombings discovered; verdict June 24, 1998; sentence 83 years.
connections: Central Park, New York – Zodiac II shooting
Woodhaven / 87th Road, Queens – Zodiac II first shooting
properties.similarities: Seda's library included a copy of Graysmith's Zodiac and trading cards on serial killers — the how-to-manual pattern that also motivated the Kobe killer.

properties.name: Tomogaoka Junior High School, Kobe, Japan – Zodiac III head scene
properties.description: Green iron front gate of the school where the severed head of Jun Hase, 11, was placed inside a plastic bag on May 24, 1997; message signed 'Seito Sakakibara' [Apostle Sake Devil Rose] and stamped with the crossed-circle symbol.
properties.summary: The signature moment of the third known Zodiac copycat, whose letters quoted Zodiac's 'I like killing people … it is so much fun' almost verbatim.
properties.financial_legal: The Japanese killer copied Zodiac's 'school children make nice targets' line; children went to school with electronic alarms.
connections: Tomogaoka Junior High School head dump site (same site)
properties.similarities: Crossed-circle symbol and misanthropic rhetoric lifted from the 1995 Japanese translation of Graysmith's Zodiac.

properties.name: Kobe, Japan
properties.description: Japanese city (~270 miles west of Tokyo) where the Zodiac III attacks occurred: a Feb 10 hammer attack on two girls, May 24 beheading of Jun Hase, and June 5 publication of a 1,400-word letter signed Seito Sakakibara.
properties.summary: The third imitator; his arrest in June 1997 at 15 years old closed the case.
connections: Tomogaoka Junior High School, Kobe, Japan – Zodiac III head scene
properties.similarities: Pacific Rim copycat — Zodiac's reach extended to Japan twenty-nine years after the original crimes.

properties.name: 225 East Utah Street, Fairfield – Paul Doerr residence
properties.description: Fairfield home attributed to Paul Alfred Doerr (per Kobek 2022). About 17 mi / 20 min from the Vallejo crime scenes.
properties.summary: Doerr's primary residence during the Zodiac era; Kobek places him in the North Bay with a Vallejo P.O. box.
properties.financial_legal: Doerr worked as a naval documents clerk; his fanzines (Hobitalia, Pioneer, Green Egg) published ciphers and an ANFO bomb formula paralleling Zodiac's.
connections: Blue Rock Springs Golf Course parking lot (Ferrin-Mageau attack)
properties.similarities: Doerr was 42 in 1969, 5'9" — consistent with witness estimates; fanzine ciphers and 1¢-stamp advocacy mirror Zodiac's habits.

properties.name: Vallejo P.O. box – Paul Doerr
properties.description: Post office box in Vallejo used by Doerr; a fanzine letter bore a Vallejo P.O. box return address.
properties.summary: The mailing address tying Doerr to the city where the first three Zodiac attacks occurred.
properties.financial_legal: Doerr advocated using only 1¢ stamps to spite the U.S. Post Office — a practice Zodiac used.
connections: 225 East Utah Street, Fairfield – Paul Doerr residence
properties.similarities: Like Allen's Burson P.O. box, a mailing address buffering residence from correspondence.

properties.name: 2377 Bush Street, San Francisco – Good Times newspaper office (Gaikowski)
properties.description: Office of the San Francisco Good Times underground newspaper, edited by Richard Gaikowski in 1969; ~1.34 mi from Mason and Geary, where Stine is thought to have picked up Zodiac.
properties.summary: Gaikowski's workplace during the murder year; a 'switchboard' associated with the paper was reportedly only yards from Stine's Fell Street residence.
properties.financial_legal: Counterculture newspaper/commune; no forensic evidence (DNA, prints, handwriting) has tied Gaikowski to the crimes.
connections: 1842 Fell Street, San Francisco – Paul Stine home
Washington & Cherry Streets, Presidio Heights (Stine murder)
Mason and Geary Streets, San Francisco
properties.similarities: Like the Avenue Theatre and the Chronicle newsroom, a counterculture media workplace within walking distance of a Zodiac crime scene.
properties.geographic: San Francisco; Bush Street, near Fillmore.

properties.name: 1842 Fell Street vicinity – Good Times 'switchboard'
properties.description: Location near Stine's Fell Street apartment where a Good Times 'switchboard' was reportedly sited, only yards from the victim's residence.
properties.summary: The proximity of a Gaikowski-linked communications point to Stine's home is one strand of the Gaikowski theory.
connections: 2377 Bush Street, San Francisco – Good Times newspaper office (Gaikowski)
1842 Fell Street, San Francisco – Paul Stine home
properties.similarities: Same proximity pattern as Allen's Fresno Street home to the Joe's Union Station booth.

properties.name: Groveland, California – Gary Francis Poste residence
properties.description: Sierra foothill town (~26 mi west of Yosemite) where Gary Francis Poste moved in 1970 and lived until his 2018 death.
properties.summary: Poste's post-murder residence and the base for the 'Posse' of young men the Case Breakers allege he recruited. Tuolumne County Sheriff Bill Pooley said local law enforcement did not take the Zodiac claim seriously.
properties.financial_legal: Air Force veteran and house painter; died 2018 at age 80.
connections: Merrell Road, Groveland – Poste arrest site
properties.similarities: Like Allen, a house painter/mechanic with firearms and a rural property; the 'Posse' echoes Zodiac-had-a-partner theories.

properties.name: Merrell Road, Groveland – Poste arrest site
properties.description: Groveland address where Poste was arrested Feb 2016 at age 78 on suspicion of corporal injury to a spouse.
properties.summary: The 2016 arrest that brought Poste back into the public record and gave the Case Breakers a documented address.
properties.financial_legal: Domestic violence charge; died 2018 before any Zodiac-related proceeding.
connections: Groveland, California – Gary Francis Poste residence
properties.similarities: Like Allen's 1974 child-molestation arrest, a non-Zodiac charge that put a suspect's address on paper.

properties.name: Riverside apartment – Rick Marshall
properties.description: Riverside apartment where Richard 'Rick' Marshall lived in 1966, close to the Cheri Jo Bates murder scene; when he vacated shortly after the murder he left a closet full of women's clothing and handbags.
properties.summary: Marshall's 1966 residence places him in the Bates crime zone. He was a ham radio operator and movie projectionist.
properties.financial_legal: No forensic evidence ever tied Marshall to the crimes. Det. Ken Narlow: 'Marshall makes good reading but [is] not a very good suspect in my estimation.'
connections: Terracina Drive (between 3680 and 3692), Riverside – Bates body site
Riverside City College – Cheri Jo Bates murder site
143 Scott Street, San Francisco – Marshall basement apartment
properties.similarities: Like Allen, present in both Southern California (1966) and San Francisco (1969) during the two crime clusters.

properties.name: 143 Scott Street, San Francisco – Marshall basement apartment
properties.description: Basement apartment where Marshall lived in 1969, a few miles from the Stine murder scene; Zodiac mentioned living in a basement.
properties.summary: The address that ties Marshall to the Stine neighborhood. He hosted a screening of Segundo de Chomón's The Red Phantom (1907) — the phrase a possible 1974 Zodiac letter used.
properties.financial_legal: Lived in a basement — matching Zodiac's 'death machine stored in my basement' phrase. Owned felt-tip pens and odd-sized paper; used a similar typewriter and teletype.
connections: Avenue Theatre, 2650 San Bruno Avenue, San Francisco
1842 Fell Street, San Francisco – Paul Stine home
properties.similarities: Basement residence, felt-tip pens, odd-sized paper, and The Red Phantom screening — four independent Marshall-Zodiac overlaps.
properties.geographic: San Francisco; Scott Street, near the Panhandle.

properties.name: Avenue Theatre, 2650 San Bruno Avenue, San Francisco
properties.description: Silent-film revival house where Marshall worked as projectionist and where black felt-tip movie posters were hand-lettered in a style closely resembling the Zodiac letters.
properties.summary: The theater whose discarded felt-tip posters may have supplied Zodiac's alphabet; its domed ceiling was painted with all the signs of the Zodiac.
properties.financial_legal: A 1932 RKO print of The Most Dangerous Game played here May 1969 — the film that inspired the Zodiac M.O.
connections: 143 Scott Street, San Francisco – Marshall basement apartment
properties.similarities: Morrill said a poster from this theater was 'the closest Zodiac lettering I've seen.'
properties.geographic: San Francisco; San Bruno Avenue, Visitacion Valley.

properties.name: Fairfield, California – William Joseph Grant residence
properties.description: Solano County city where William Joseph Grant, the suspect pursued by CHP officer Lyndon Lafferty and (under a pseudonym) by Graysmith, lived during the Zodiac era.
properties.summary: Grant's residence and the location of the 'road games' Lafferty experienced with a vehicle later believed to be Grant's car being used by Zodiac.
properties.financial_legal: Grant's DNA reportedly failed 3 of 5 criteria, with 2 of 5 identical — an inconclusive comparison. Died Feb 2012.
connections: Blue Rock Springs Golf Course parking lot (Ferrin-Mageau attack)
properties.similarities: Like Allen, a Fairfield/Vallejo-area man with a car and firearms; the 'road games' echo Zodiac's highway stalking.

properties.name: Spahn Ranch, Simi Valley – Manson Family base (Bruce Davis)
properties.description: Former movie set outside Los Angeles that served as the Manson Family's primary residence 1968–69, including Bruce Davis, later named by some researchers as a Zodiac suspect.
properties.summary: Davis's residence during the Zodiac murder year. He was in the San Francisco area at the time of the killings and is sometimes linked to the 1970 disappearance of coed Robin Graham.
properties.financial_legal: Davis convicted of the 1969 murders of Gary Hinman and Donald 'Shorty' Shea; was in the Bay Area during the Zodiac period. No forensic evidence ties him to Zodiac.
connections: 636 Cole Street, San Francisco – Manson residence 1967
properties.similarities: Like the 'Zodiac was a Manson associate' theories, Davis fits the cult-killing adjacency but lacks any physical link.

properties.name: 636 Cole Street, San Francisco – Manson Family residence (1967)
properties.description: Haight-Ashbury address where Charles Manson lived in 1967, about 2.5 mi from the San Francisco Examiner; Bruce Davis and other Family members were in the neighborhood during the Zodiac period.
properties.summary: The Haight-Ashbury base that put the Manson Family in the same city as the Stine murder and the Zodiac letter campaign.
connections: Spahn Ranch, Simi Valley – Manson Family base (Bruce Davis)
properties.similarities: Same geographic overlap as Allen's Fresno Street and Marshall's Scott Street residences.

properties.name: Sherwood Morrill residence – Wallace Penny visit
properties.description: Morrill's Sacramento home where Wallace Penny ('Penny' in Graysmith's book) arrived unannounced with his wife, hands shaking, claiming to know Zodiac and naming Don Andrews.
properties.summary: The doorstep where the most persistent private-citizen theory in the case was first delivered to the state's top handwriting examiner.
properties.financial_legal: Penny brought handprinting samples he attributed to Andrews; Morrill found some matches but not enough to identify.
properties.similarities: Like Cheney's 1971 tip, a citizen-initiated lead that consumed years of investigative time.

properties.name: Copper Penny restaurant, San Francisco
properties.description: San Francisco restaurant where Graysmith and Dave Toschi met repeatedly over lemon meringue pie and french fries to discuss the 2,500 Zodiac suspects.
properties.summary: The informal meeting place for the case's longest-running detective-author collaboration.
properties.similarities: Like the Owl and Monkey Cafe where Graysmith wrote, a recurring off-the-record case hub.

properties.name: 'Jack' apartment – 1979 Hell's Angels-adjacent roommate
properties.description: Apartment of the suspect Graysmith called 'Jack' (a tall, thin, bald former policeman who had taken crime-scene photos of Darlene Ferrin as souvenirs). Graysmith visited him in 1979; his fingerprints did not match the bloody Stine cab print.
properties.summary: The 1979 suspect who had been a Vallejo-area lawman and possessed official Ferrin crime-scene photos; ruled out by prints and physical appearance.
properties.financial_legal: Had been fired from a sheriff's department; owned crime-scene photos he admitted taking as 'souvenirs.'
connections: Blue Rock Springs Golf Course parking lot (Ferrin-Mageau attack)
properties.similarities: A police-groupie suspect with access to evidence — the same profile as the Zodiac-as-cop theories.

properties.name: Dr. Thomas Rykoff office, Santa Rosa
properties.description: Santa Rosa psychiatric office where Dr. Rykoff evaluated Arthur Leigh Allen as a condition of parole, and later hypnotized Allen's sister-in-law Karen Allen, who drew Zodiac-like symbols under trance.
properties.summary: Where the most detailed post-1977 psychological material on Allen was generated, including the sister-in-law's automatic-writing session.
properties.financial_legal: Rykoff was retained as a favor to Husted and Allen's parole officer; eventually fled to a wilderness hospital, telling Bawart he feared Allen would kill him.
connections: 32 Fresno Street, Vallejo – Arthur Leigh Allen home
properties.similarities: The hypnosis session with Karen Allen produced grid-like symbols resembling the 340 cipher's third line — the most specific Rykoff-era clue.

properties.name: Day Street, Noe Valley – Don Cheney residence (1965–66)
properties.description: San Francisco Noe Valley address where Donald Lee Cheney lived from early 1965 until late 1965 or early 1966, giving him familiarity with the North Bay and Presidio Heights.
properties.summary: Cheney's first Bay Area residence, before his move to Concord; it placed him near the future Stine murder neighborhood.
connections: Halifax Way, Concord – Don Cheney residence (1966–69)
1842 Fell Street, San Francisco – Paul Stine home
properties.similarities: A future key witness living within a few miles of a Zodiac crime scene — the same geographic coincidence that later made Allen a suspect.

properties.name: Halifax Way, Concord – Don Cheney residence (1966–Jan 1969)
properties.description: Concord address where Cheney lived from early 1966 until he moved to Southern California in Jan 1969; ~13 mi from Lake Herman Road and 7 from Blue Rock Springs.
properties.summary: The residence from which Cheney commuted to Cal Poly Pomona and where he had his New Year's Day 1969 conversation with Allen in Vallejo.
connections: Day Street, Noe Valley – Don Cheney residence (1965–66)
La Vitta Avenue, Pomona – Don Cheney residence (1969–71)
properties.similarities: Cheney lived 13 mi from the first Zodiac murder site and 7 from the second — proximity that made his account of Allen's 'Zodiac' conversation especially significant.

properties.name: La Vitta Avenue, Pomona – Don Cheney residence (1969–71)
properties.description: Pomona house Cheney bought after moving to Southern California in Jan 1969; about a 6.5-hour drive from the Bay Area.
properties.summary: Cheney's Southern California residence during three of the four canonical Zodiac crimes; his move here is why he did not come forward until 1971.
properties.financial_legal: New job at Fluor engineering in Pomona.
connections: Halifax Way, Concord – Don Cheney residence (1966–Jan 1969)
properties.similarities: The move that delayed his tip — a geographic gap the defense could have exploited if Allen had been tried.

properties.name: Pomona police station – Cheney's first report
properties.description: Pomona Police Department where Cheney first reported his suspicions about Allen in early 1971; the report was apparently never forwarded.
properties.summary: The first official report of the Allen-Zodiac theory — a lead that nearly vanished before Panzarella pushed Cheney to call Manhattan Beach PD.
connections: La Vitta Avenue, Pomona – Don Cheney residence (1969–71)
properties.similarities: Like the Concerned Citizen's 1969 letter to Sgt. Lynch, a citizen report that was under-processed and nearly lost.
